column4: Visit note | 2026-02-17 03:30 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Shapla Sarkar, 70, female. Mrs. Sarkar presents for a first visit having no current physical symptoms, but mentions that her father had a heart attack at 55. She discovered high cholesterol levels during an office health check in Bogura. She works as a madrasa teacher and leads a largely sedentary lifestyle. She reports no chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath on exertion. On examination: LDL cholesterol 4.3 mmol/L, BP 125/75 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 77 kg. Heart sounds are dual with no murmurs, and lung fields are clear. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat lipid profile.
